thread:
amanda: quick follow-up from the RFC review — we need to pick choreography vs orchestration for the continuous batcher refactor. thoughts?
chris: +1 we should list concrete tradeoffs. choreography reduces single-point-of-decision but increases cross-service coupling.
sanjay: also ordering and replay are harder with choreography. do we have deterministic replay infra?
lia: not today. we have event logging but no deterministic replayer for the batch scheduler. building that is non-trivial.
amanda: summary proposal: adopt a hybrid model. choreography for lightweight admission and signaling, orchestration (conductor) for deadline/fallback decisions. keeps fastpath elastic, centralizes policy decisions that require global view.
chris: sounds pragmatic. main risks: visibility + debugging, and race between signals. how do we observe causal chains?
sanjay: we can attach a 128-bit trace id to every enqueue/evict/admit event and write a compact event record to kafka. then build a consumer that materializes the causal graph for traces.
lia: perf impact? extra I/O on enqueue path. microbench showed ~0.8ms median and 3ms p95 overhead when we log synchronously. async batch-write drops that to ~0.2ms median, ~1ms p95.
amanda: let's keep logging async. telemetry required: enqueue->batch latency, admission decisions, reorder rate, fallback triggers, and kv-cache warmup misses.
chris: interface boundary question: what does an "admission signal" look like? lightweight token vs full request object?
sanjay: propose a small immutable token containing: trace_id, tenant_id, token_len, deadline_ns, qos_hint. full request stays local to runtime. token is what flows through the choreography bus.
lia: +1. token reduces payload copying and avoids exposing internal request shape across services.
amanda: example token proto we discussed:
```
message AdmissionToken {
  string trace_id = 1;
  string tenant_id = 2;
  uint32 token_len = 3;
  int64 deadline_ns = 4;
  enum QoS { LOW=0, NORMAL=1, HIGH=2 } qos = 5;
}
```
chris: good. next: failure modes. if an event is lost or delayed we need deterministic fallback paths. conductor should be able to re-evaluate missing signals after timeout.
sanjay: implement a "pessimistic timeout" that promotes local fallback at T_timeout = min(remaining_deadline/3, 50ms). conductor can override later if it receives late signals.
lia: ordering: clusters with clock skew can reorder events. include monotonic sequence numbers per-host and rely on trace_id+seq for causal ordering. reconciliation job will detect conflicting orders and emit alerts.
amanda: rollout plan: 1) wire token-instrumentation + async event log on dev cluster for 2 weeks; 2) run passive choreography (emit events but still use central orchestrator path) and collect telemetry for 4 weeks; 3) enable hybrid for 5% of traffic on canary hosts; 4) ramp with health checks.
chris: what health checks? failure budget?
sanjay: metrics to gate: p50/p95 enqueue latency, tail-latency of first-token-to-batch, reorder_rate, fallback_rate, successful_replays. set hard abort if p95 enqueue increases >15% or fallback_rate >2x baseline.
lia: add a canary smoke test: deterministic-request set that validates identical outputs between old and new paths. run once per deploy.
amanda: owner: runtime/scheduler team (chris), infra to provide event bus + consumer (sanjay), devex to add trace visuals (lia). I'll own rollout coordination.
chris: small implementation notes: prefer single-threaded appenders per host to reduce seq contention, use a ring buffer for in-memory batching, flush on either batch size or 5ms.
sanjay: also add idempotency tokens on the conductor side so replaying events is safe.
lia: docs note: update obs dashboards: add a "choreography visibility" dashboard showing live inflight traces, avg events/sec, and late-event queue length.
amanda: timeline: prototype 2 weeks, passive 4 weeks, canary 2 weeks per stage. total ~10-12 weeks.
chris: tradeoffs recap in one line: choreography = lower latency & faster local decisions, orchestration = easier correctness & global policy. hybrid = pragmatic compromise.
sanjay: open question: do we risk vendor lock-in by depending on our Kafka cluster? maybe add pluggable event sink (kafka | s3+lambda) interface.
lia: pluggable is fine, but for rollout we need stable low-latency sink. kafka default.
amanda: action items: @chris implement token + async logger prototype; @sanjay spin up consumer prototype and materializer; @lia draft obs dashboard and smoke test harness; I'll draft a short RFC addendum with rollout gating thresholds.
chris: ack. starting prototype today.
deploy-bot: Canary started: choreography-refactor-prototype on cluster batch-dev-3 (canary id=cr-2026-04-22-1) :rocket:
sanjay: noted — will watch the consumer lag metric and alert on >5s lag.
lia: adding checklist to the PR for tests and dashboards. :memo:
amanda: thanks team — we'll sync next Wed for initial telemetry review. :thumbsup:
